Facility Inventory & Condition Assessmen.justification: Comprehensive district-wide inventory including detailed building sizes, ages, portables, and specialized spaces; robust condition assessment covering HVAC, roofing, electrical, plumbing, lighting, technology infrastructure, and accessibility; uses multiple data sources including field assessments and urgency timelines; connects condition data to student outcomes and long-term capital planning (Chapters 2, 5, Facility Assessments, Project Prioritization).

Enrollment & Capacity Planning.justification: Provides detailed enrollment history and projections over 15+ years with demographic context; includes capacity utilization data by site and classroom; links enrollment trends to specific facility actions such as portable replacements, new buildings, and site expansions; discusses boundary changes and adaptive uses (Sections 1.6, 5.1, individual site plans).

Educational Alignment.justification: Educational alignment is a core organizing principle with guiding principles for design explicitly linked to educational goals; detailed educational adequacy assessments; facility projects directly respond to educational needs including collaborative spaces, 21st-century learning environments, technology integration, and program-specific requirements (Chapters 1.8, 2.3, site-specific educational adequacy discussions).

Outdoor Spaces & Greening.justification: Includes data and analysis of outdoor spaces with references to turf and shrub reduction programs for drought tolerance; identifies strategies such as shade structures, amphitheaters, outdoor learning spaces, and improved site circulation; however, greening strategies are not fully districtwide or deeply detailed (Site observations and recommendations across multiple schools, e.g., Blue Oak, Oak Meadow, Silva Valley).

Climate Risk & Mitigation.justification: Acknowledges sustainability and drought-tolerant landscaping as part of site work; however, no comprehensive climate risk assessment or detailed climate resilience strategies are presented; climate readiness is not a central theme (Guiding Principles mention sustainability, but no detailed climate risk assessment found).

Energy Efficiency & Resilience.justification: Mentions energy efficiency projects such as HVAC replacements and solar PV at newest school; lacks comprehensive energy data or detailed strategies for electrification, decarbonization, or energy resilience; no explicit reference to state mandates like Title 24 or Zero Net Energy goals (Facility assessments note HVAC upgrades and PV at Valley View).

Financial Plan & Capital Strategy.justification: Presents detailed cost estimates by project and urgency with escalation and contingencies; clear project prioritization framework with categories linked to funding availability; outlines multiple funding sources including state programs, bonds, developer fees; discusses long-term financial sustainability and district capacity; includes district facility cost estimates and funding challenges (Chapter 5, Project Costs, Funding Opportunities).
